summary_html: Court issues a **protective or restraining order** to prevent contact, remove abuser, or ensure safety without removing the child. Federal law leaves implementation to states but funds protection efforts through CAPTA and IV-B.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — authorizes protective interventions and state plan requirements  
- **SSA Title IV-B** — permits funding for protective services and court interventions

primary_citations.citation_text: Wyoming - Wyo. Stat. §§ 14-3-201 through 14-3-216 (Article 2, Child Protective Services – § 14-3-205(a) duty to report, which applies to any person)
Wyoming - Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-401 et seq. (Child Protection Act – juvenile court process for abuse and neglect)
Title 14: Children - DFS - CHILD WELFARE PRIMARY

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed the neglect adjudication, holding the State must prove neglect by a preponderance of the evidence, and cautioned that an officer taking warrantless protective custody under Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 14-3-405(a)(i) must actually find the child seriously endangered rather than apply a blanket positive-drug-test policy.
key_cases.relevance: Shows the court's power to order continued shelter care as the protective measure short of adjudication.
key_cases.quote: During the adjudicatory hearing, the State had the burden to prove its allegations of neglect by a preponderance of the evidence

key_cases.holding: The Court reversed, holding the juvenile court violated the father's due-process right to notice and an opportunity to be heard in the early stages of the case, and that 'other aggravating circumstances' relieving the Department of reasonable efforts under Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 14-2-309(c)(v) must be as severe as the enumerated grounds.
key_cases.relevance: Shows the limits on protective orders and placements entered without hearing the absent parent.
key_cases.quote: the legislature logically meant for “other aggravating circumstances” to meet the same level of severity as set out in the preceding provisions

key_cases.case_name: Matter of Termination of Parental Rights to ALRW
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed termination under Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 14-2-309(a)(iii), holding that the sufficiency of the Department's reasonable efforts is assessed case by case and that the Department must tie its efforts to the reasons that necessitated the child's out-of-home placement.
key_cases.relevance: Illustrates the protective steps, including suspended visitation, ordered short of termination.
key_cases.quote: We assess whether sufficient evidence supports that DFS made reasonable efforts to rehabilitate the family on a case-by-case basis

state_agency.name: Wyoming Department of Family Services
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the DFS field office in the county where the child lives — the list is at dfs.wyo.gov/about/contact-us

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives

timeline_requirements.deadline: 48 hours, excluding weekends and legal holidays
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Child taken into temporary protective custody
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in statute; full-time shelter care continues only if the court finds at the hearing that it is required (Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-409(a), (d))

parent_rights_at_moment: Right to know where child is going
Right to a shelter care hearing as soon as reasonably possible and no later than 48 hours, excluding weekends and legal holidays (Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-409(a))
A DFS caseworker cannot take your child: only a law enforcement officer, a treating physician, physician's assistant or nurse practitioner, or a court order can (Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-405)
what_to_say: Do you have a court order for removal?
What is the specific imminent danger?
Where are you taking my child?
what_not_to_do: Do not physically interfere with lawful removal
